correctness.rationale: The signed 105-by-105 chain boundary and canonical cycle are reconstructed independently. An included 105-entry integral primal vector has boundary precisely \(3z\) with l1 norm 28. The included rational dual (integer thirds) has coboundary infinity norm at most one and pairs to 28 with 3z, proving global real/integral optimality. Exact F3 elimination shows z nonzero modulo boundaries. Exhaustive 945-cycle enumeration plus the transitive 630-cycle orbit prove the global classification.

broader_coverage.reasoning: These results give stronger homological *group classification* and canonical generators, but do not determine minimal chain-filling costs. An isomorphism of integral homology does not constrain the l1 norm of a particular chain filling. The proposed norm statement is not a corollary of their abstract homology isomorphisms.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The earlier picture is evidence for a finite filling, not a universal sharp lower bound. A new dual inequality quantifies all real or integral fillings, even those unrelated to the historical pictured surface. The cycle orbit classification makes the bound apply simultaneously to all shortest essential simple cycles. This is a metric-on-chains refinement that is not implied by the published abstract torsion calculation.

originality.rationale: Known work establishes 3-torsion and gives a bounding surface, but not a sharp universal l1 norm for every shortest torsion generator. The dual lower certificate proves an additional statement not implied by prior homology group calculations or the published existence of a surface.
residual_risks: The original Bouc 1992 full article was not separately accessible/inspected in full; the 2004 open primary paper reproduces its relevant construction and theorem.
Unindexed manuscripts or alternate combinatorial formulations may give the sharp filling lower bound; failure to locate one is not a proof of priority.
The classification concerns simplest homologically essential loops and the l1 norm for exactly three times those loops, not broader relative filling profiles.

value.rationale: For the first classical matching complex with 3-torsion, the least chain area required to fill three times a shortest nontrivial loop is a natural torsion isoperimetric invariant. Its sharp value 28, accompanied by complete classification of all 945 simple four-cycles and a portable exact primal/dual proof, is structurally motivated and not an arbitrary parameter sample. The result does not claim a general asymptotic bound.
